memory_update.text: SPSC should be carried forward as the highest-purity underfollowed candidate for retail supplier connectivity, EDI, compliance logic, and operational switching-cost research.

Retail supplier connectivity networks should be evaluated on recurring-revenue quality, trading-partner count, retailer coverage, compliance-map depth, implementation cycles, retention, and organic growth rather than only headline SaaS growth.

DSGX and OTEX are plausible second-order infrastructure candidates, but both need segment-level verification because retail EDI exposure is embedded inside broader logistics, compliance, or enterprise software portfolios.

Private competitors such as TrueCommerce and other EDI/VAN providers may define the competitive set but are not directly US-listed; later layers should map private competitors to public acquirers, integration partners, or customers.

summary: Expanded the universe around scarce retail connectivity infrastructure rather than consumer brands. The strongest underfollowed fit is SPS Commerce because its disclosed positioning centers on a retail supply-chain network, recurring-revenue customers, and embedded trading-partner workflows. Descartes and OpenText are plausible second-order infrastructure providers via B2B connectivity, EDI, compliance, and trading-partner networks, but their exposure is broader and less pure. Manhattan Associates is included as a reference/adjacent order-management infrastructure name rather than a pure EDI network. No buy/sell recommendation is made.
